title: JENGA: Enhancing LLM Long-Context Fine-tuning with Contextual Token Sparsity
note: LLM fine-tuning system exploiting contextual token sparsity to cut activation memory; artifact minimum is a single A800 or A40 GPU so smaller OPT/Llama models fit the 24 GB A5000. Concern: scalability experiments used 4x 4090 and long-context runs may need memory scale-down

title: An Empirical Evaluation of Columnar Storage Formats
note: Parquet-ORC storage-format deep dive with a released benchmark harness; C++/Arrow builds in user space, GPU-decode part optional

title: RollPacker: Taming Long-Tail Rollouts for RL Post-Training with Tail Batching
note: Tail batching - a rollout scheduling policy for synchronous RL post-training; the policy itself is workload-level and can be studied with a 0.5-1.5B model on one GPU or replayed in simulation. Concern - the paper's speedups are measured on multi-GPU veRL and SGLang deployments of Qwen2.5 models.

title: CDLM: Consistency Diffusion Language Models for Faster Sampling
note: Diffusion-LM sampling acceleration with block-causal masks that restore KV-cache compatibility - pure inference-side systems angle. Concern: the consistency fine-tuning stage targets 7-8B diffusion LMs and likely needs more than one 24 GB GPU; released checkpoints make the inference/KV-cache half reproducible on the A5000

title: Mnemosyne: Dynamic Workload-Aware BF Tuning via Accurate Statistics in LSM trees
note: Workload-aware Bloom filter memory allocation in LSM-trees; user-space KV store

title: Fast Vector Query Processing for Large Datasets Beyond GPU Memory with Reordered Pipelining
note: GPU-accelerated billion-scale ANN vector search; the paper itself uses a single A100 and streams vectors from host RAM, so the mechanism is single-GPU. User-space CUDA on a Faiss fork. Concern: paper used 40 GB GPU and 1152 GB host RAM for billion-scale sets - on 24 GB GPU plus 125 GiB RAM and 257 GB free disk the study must scale down to 100M-scale datasets. CUDA toolkit newer than 11.8 would need a conda install.

title: BWoS: Formally Verified Block-based Work Stealing for Parallel Processing
note: User-space concurrency library: block-partitioned work-stealing deques for language runtimes, evaluated with Renaissance on Java GC, Go JSON processing and the Rust Tokio HTTP server - all runnable on 16 cores with no root. Concern: the artifact received FUNCTIONAL and REPRODUCED badges but no AVAILABLE badge; the code that is public is the authors' Tokio fork branch referenced from the paper (Tokio PR tokio-rs/tokio#5283), which contains the bwosq implementation but is not a packaged artifact, and the Java/Go integrations are not obviously released. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/jschwe/tokio-rs/tree/bwos_master_lib .

title: OrbitFlow: SLO-Aware Long-Context LLM Serving with Fine-Grained KV Cache Reconfiguration
note: SLO-aware per-layer KV cache placement between GPU and host memory with an ILP solver and runtime refinement; a single-GPU serving problem

title: FLOWS: Balanced MRC Profiling for Heterogeneous Object-Size Cache
note: Spatial-sampling MRC profiler that fixes byte-miss-ratio error for variable-object-size (CDN) traces. Trace-driven, user-space, no hardware requirements. Pairs naturally with TTLs Matter as a two-paper comparison target

title: Kamino: Efficient VM Allocation at Scale with Latency-Driven Cache-Aware Scheduling
note: Cache-aware request-scheduling algorithm evaluated with a high-fidelity simulator on production traces - simulation-only, so it fits the machine. Concern on code: the artifact carries Available + Functional + Reproduced badges on the OSDI '25 AE results page, but the PDF contains no repository URL, the authors' project page (daviddomingo.com/projects/Kamino) says "more information to be released", and GitHub search found nothing - repo marked unknown rather than out-no-code. Second concern: the Azure production traces are likely not public.

title: Leveraging Dynamic and Heterogeneous Workload Knowledge to Boost the Performance of Index Advisors
note: learning-based index advisor for dynamic and heterogeneous workloads

title: SHIELD: Encrypting Persistent Data of LSM-KVS from Monolithic to Disaggregated Storage
note: Encryption design for LSM key-value store persistent data; monolithic deployment runs on one machine, concern - the disaggregated setup needs two nodes

title: A New Paradigm in Tuning Learned Indexes: A Reinforcement Learning Enhanced Approach
note: RL-based end-to-end tuner for learned index structures; user space

title: Towards Optimal Transaction Scheduling
note: schedule-first concurrency control and greedy schedule search implemented in RocksDB; single machine

title: LeaFTL: A Learning-Based Flash Translation Layer for Solid-State Drives
note: Learned-index flash translation layer - ships a trace-driven SSD simulator that runs in user space; concern the full FEMU setup wants KVM which is unavailable

title: Plexus: Optimizing Join Approximation for Geo-Distributed Data Analytics
note: Join-sampling algorithms plus weight approximation and heterogeneity-aware allocation; the artifact is a Scala/sbt client-server program, so the algorithmic contribution is testable as several user-space processes. Concern: the setting is wide-area - realistic WAN emulation normally needs tc/netem, which requires root, so latency/bandwidth heterogeneity would have to be injected in application code; borderline, flagged for the audit stage.

title: Scarf: Self-Adaptive Tuning via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning for Apache Flink
note: Multi-objective RL configuration tuning for Apache Flink. Concern: Flink must be run as a local multi-process cluster and throughput numbers will not match a real cluster

title: Learning-Augmented Competitive Algorithms for Spatiotemporal Online Allocation with Deadline Constraints (ST-CLIP)
note: Carbon-aware spatiotemporal scheduling of delay-tolerant batch jobs across datacenters, evaluated as a trace-driven simulation (carbon-intensity traces) in Python/Jupyter - no cluster or root needed. Concern: primarily an online-algorithms paper (competitive ratio, consistency-robustness trade-off); the artifact is a notebook-based simulation harness, so the project would be a policy/prediction improvement rather than a systems build.

title: FastGL: A GPU-Efficient Framework for Accelerating Sampling-Based GNN Training at Large Scale
note: GPU-efficient sampling, memory-IO and computation pipeline for large-scale GNN training on a single GPU with host-memory graph storage.

title: ACGraph: An Efficient Asynchronous Out-of-Core Graph Processing Framework
note: asynchronous out-of-core graph engine for SSD with block-centric I/O scheduling - user-space I/O systems work - concern: graph-analytics flavour and no repo found

title: MAGIS: Memory Optimization via Coordinated Graph Transformation and Scheduling for DNN
note: Coordinated graph transformation plus scheduling for DNN memory reduction; single-GPU, and memory-constrained studies are a natural fit for a 24 GB card.

title: A Data Optimizer for Region-Aware Self-describing Files in Scientific Computing (RASTER)
note: User-space C++ middleware that reorganizes self-describing (HDF5/NetCDF-style) files into region-aware variable groups - runs entirely in user space over ordinary files. Concern - the paper's three evaluation platforms are Optane PMEM, Huawei OceanStor and Sunway TaihuLight; none are available, so the study would have to be re-baselined on local NVMe, which changes the headline speedups.

title: DOTE: Rethinking (Predictive) WAN Traffic Engineering
note: Deep-learning replacement for demand prediction in WAN traffic engineering - training and evaluation are entirely offline on released topologies and traces and fit one A5000 - Concern: the domain is network traffic engineering rather than core OS and reproducing the LP baselines needs a solver such as Gurobi

title: Balancing Fairness and Performance in Multi-User Spark Workloads with Dynamic Scheduling
note: User Weighted Fair Queuing plus runtime partitioning, implemented as a patched Spark 3.5.5 (JVM, entirely user space) with a companion benchmark tool and a Zenodo artifact. Concern - the original evaluation uses a multi-node cluster; on this machine it must be reproduced with a single-host standalone Spark deployment and multiple executors across the 32 threads. Java must be installed via conda.

title: Diffusion-Based Generative System Surrogates for Scalable Learning-Driven Optimization in Virtual Playgrounds (DiffNEST)
note: Diffusion model that generates synthetic system traces so that RL-based system optimizers can be trained without physical hardware; Python/PyTorch, single-GPU training fits 24 GB. Repo URL is stated in the abstract, so it is unambiguously official. Concerns: the two case studies (task-aware adaptive DVFS, multi-core cache partitioning) actuate hardware knobs that need root here - DVFS via cpupower and CAT/pqos are both blocked - so only the surrogate-training and offline-evaluation half is reproducible; repo is small and was pushed only once (Mar 2025).

title: NEST: Network- and Memory-Aware Device Placement for Distributed Deep Learning
note: Dynamic-programming device-placement planner that jointly models network, compute and memory; the planner itself is a user-space solver that can be studied and improved offline. Concern: validating the predicted throughput needs real multi-GPU clusters, so the project would have to stay in the planner/simulation half

title: Themis: Detecting Distributed Concurrency Bugs through RPC-Driven Race-Directed Test Generation and Fuzzing
note: Static race detection plus LLM-generated tests plus directed fuzzing for distributed concurrency bugs - the eight target systems run as local processes; no root, no special hardware. Concern - the LLM test-generation stage needs an external API budget or a local model.

title: Ahead-of-time Analysis of Shell Program Effects
note: SaSh statically analyzes shell scripts with optimistic symbolic execution over a filesystem model. Pure user-space CPU work - no GPU, no root. Official repo found under the authors Brown lab org. Very good fit for a 10-week improvement project (precision or speed of the symbolic engine is directly measurable).

title: AgileLog: A Forkable Shared Log for Agents on Data Streams
note: Forkable shared-log abstraction plus the Bolt implementation. User-space C++ log server. Concern: shared logs are normally evaluated on a multi-node cluster - here it would have to be many processes on one host. Repo is the authors lab org (dassl-uiuc) and is public but named -Proto so it may be a prototype rather than the final artifact.

title: Taming Dynamism on GPUs: Cross-SM Kernel Fusion via SM Cooperation and Just-in-Time Reduction
note: MorphKernel fuses multi-phase dynamic GPU operators (decode attention, MoE expert activation) across SMs with fine-grained SM synchronization. Single GPU by construction. Strong concern: third-party notes say the implementation uses TMA send and recv primitives and GPC-topology-aware communication, which are Hopper sm_90 features - the A5000 is Ampere sm_86 and has no TMA, so a port would be substantial.

title: Rajomon: Decentralized and Coordinated Overload Control for Latency-Sensitive Microservices
note: Pure user-space Go/gRPC interceptor library implementing a token-and-price admission-control / rate-limiting policy; a resource manager that can be studied as many processes on one host. Concern: paper evaluates on up to 140 cores across a cluster; on 16C/32T the microservice graphs (DeathStarBench-style) must be scaled down, and load generators compete with the services for cores.

title: DIGRA: A Dynamic Graph Indexing for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search with Range Filter
note: Dynamic graph index for range-filtered ANN; single machine

title: LOFT: A Lock-free and Adaptive Learned Index with High Scalability for Dynamic Workloads
note: Lock-free learned index with non-blocking retraining; in-memory user-space C++ and a 32-thread scalability study matches this machine exactly. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - the paper may use higher core counts than 16 cores and 32 threads, so scalability claims will have to be re-plotted at smaller thread counts

title: Blaze: Compiling JSON Schema for 10x Faster Validation
note: Ahead-of-time compilation of JSON Schema into a fast validation representation with a 10x speedup; user-space C++ compiler and runtime with a public benchmark artifact

title: Bridging the Gap between Relational OLTP and Graph-based OLAP (GART)
note: In-memory user-space system; the core contributions (mutable CSR, coarse-grained MVCC versioning, flexible property store) are data-structure/locality work measurable with wall-clock timing on one node. Code released both as SJTU-IPADS/vegito branch gart (AE link) and the maintained GraphScope/GART. Concerns: depends on the large Vineyard/GraphScope stack; LDBC SNB dataset generation is time-consuming.

title: RapidStore: An Efficient Dynamic Graph Storage System for Concurrent Queries
note: Concurrency-optimized in-memory dynamic graph store with decoupled version data; multicore user-space system

title: Zeno Filter: To Infinity in Tiny Steps
note: in-place expandable filter that grows by less than 2x - compact storage data structure - concern: no repo located

title: Atom: An Efficient Query Serving System for Embedding-based Knowledge Graph Reasoning with Operator-level Batching
note: Operator-level batching and scheduling for an embedding-model query serving system; single-GPU serving workload

title: The Art of Latency Hiding in Modern Database Engines
note: stackless coroutines plus scheduling to hide I/O and synchronization latency in an OLTP engine; user-space C++, no root

title: Scalable Model-Based Management of Massive High Frequency Wind Turbine Data with ModelarDB
note: model-based time-series compression evaluation in Rust. Concern: the edge-to-cloud pipeline must be collapsed onto one host

title: Ken: An Execution Engine for Unstructured Database Systems
note: Execution engine that adapts model cascades to query load while managing GPU memory and data movement. Concern: model sizes must be kept within 24 GB

title: Swift: Fast Performance Tuning with GAN-Generated Configurations
note: Bayesian-optimization tuner that uses a GAN to generate candidate configurations for big-data systems; the tuner itself is user-space Python and can be driven by surrogates or traces. Concern: the paper tuned 4-node Flink and 8-node Spark clusters, so on-machine evaluation must use local-mode or simulated targets

title: hS: Speculative Script Reordering at Subprocess Granularity
note: Out-of-order speculative execution of shell scripts with runtime effect detection; user-space, no root, benchmarks are local shell pipelines. Zenodo archive 10.5281/zenodo.19832407; artifact-eval branch osdi26-ae. Concern: effect interception may rely on user namespaces/overlayfs - available here, but worth confirming

title: CaaS-LSM: Compaction-as-a-Service for LSM-based Key-Value Stores in Storage Disaggregated Infrastructure
note: LSM compaction offloading built on RocksDB. Concern: the design targets storage-disaggregated deployments (separate compute/storage nodes, container orchestration) - on one machine it can only be emulated with multiple processes

title: Boggart: Towards General-Purpose Acceleration of Retrospective Video Analytics
note: Retrospective video analytics accelerator combining classical CV indices with sparing CNN invocation - runs as user-space Python on one GPU - Concern: needs large video corpora to be downloaded into the 257 GB of free space and depends on older CUDA-era PyTorch and OpenCV builds

title: Understanding and Detecting Query Performance Regression in Practical Index Tuning: [Experiments & Analysis]
note: study and pattern-based detector for query performance regression caused by index tuning - learned/heuristic component of an auto-indexing service - concern: built around Azure SQL and the what-if API - code likely not released

title: HyperGef: A Framework Enabling Efficient Fusion for Hypergraph Neural Network on GPUs
note: Fused GPU kernels and a workload-aware sparse format for hypergraph neural networks - single-GPU kernel work compared against cuSPARSE - concern - graph datasets must be sized to 24 GB and the kernels may need retuning for Ampere consumer-class shared memory

title: MorphStream: Adaptive Scheduling for Scalable Transactional Stream Processing on Multicores
note: Adaptive decomposition and scheduling of state transactions across cores - explicitly a multicore scheduling paper with a maintained Java artifact; fits 16C/32T perfectly

title: FreshGNN: Reducing Memory Access via Stable Historical Embeddings for Graph Neural Network Training
note: historical-embedding cache policy that cuts feature loading in GNN mini-batch training; single-GPU configuration exists

title: High-Throughput Ingestion for Video Warehouse: Comprehensive Configuration and Effective Exploration
note: Configuration search for video ingestion pipelines with model selection; single-GPU video analytics

title: AlloyStack: A Library Operating System for Serverless Workflow Applications
note: User-space library OS that shares one address space across serverless workflow functions and isolates them with MPK; the target CPU reports the pku and ospke flags so unprivileged pkey_alloc works. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - needs a Rust toolchain, and the Firecracker or gVisor style baselines need KVM or root so only the LibOS side is reproducible

title: Efficient Large Graph Processing with Chunk-Based Graph Representation Model
note: I/O-efficient out-of-core graph engine on NVMe SSDs - a pure user-space C++ system on hardware we have, with I/O amplification and runtime as improvable metrics. Concern: the largest graphs in the paper approach or exceed our 257 GB of free space, so the study must use the smaller datasets

title: GLogS: Interactive Graph Pattern Matching Query At Large Scale
note: User-space declarative query compiler plus cost-based optimizer on top of a dataflow engine; the headline 51x-over-Neo4j result is a single-machine number, so the optimizer can be studied without a cluster. Rust/Java toolchain is installable in user space. Concerns: the scalability half of the evaluation is distributed (16 machines) and cannot be reproduced; large LDBC datasets need tens of GB of the ~257 GB free.

title: High-Performance DBMSs with io_uring: When and How to Use It
note: Systematic study of io_uring in a buffer manager and in network shuffling with concrete design guidelines; user-space Linux I O work. Concern: NVMe passthrough experiments may need device permissions this account lacks

title: Udon: Efficient Debugging of User-Defined Functions in Big Data Systems with Line-by-Line Control
note: User-space debugger for UDFs in a data-processing engine; JVM/Python, no root. Concern: needs a Scala/Java toolchain installed in user space

title: Revisiting the Design of In-Memory Dynamic Graph Storage
note: Common abstraction plus generic test framework for in-memory dynamic graph storage; strong reproduction/improvement target on one machine

title: Serving and Optimizing Machine Learning Workflows on Heterogeneous Infrastructures
note: ML-workflow serving and placement optimizer. Concern: original evaluation spans an edge-cloud heterogeneous cluster - on one host it must run as co-located processes or the placement optimizer studied offline from profiles

title: InfiniFilter: Expanding Filters to Infinity and Beyond
note: Filter that expands capacity while keeping a false-positive bound - the filter component of LSM key-value stores; Java artifact, CPU only

title: Batched in Back: Characterizing and Optimizing Offline LLM Inference in Production with ACDC
note: Offline (batch) LLM inference characterization and optimization. Offline batching is a natural single-GPU workload and scheduling ideas port down easily. Concern: it is a production study at Alibaba so the traces and the 7B-plus model fleet may not be released - the optimization part may still be reproducible on one GPU.

title: MoDM: Efficient Serving for Image Generation via Mixture-of-Diffusion Models
note: Caching-based serving for diffusion models; retrieval cache plus small/large model mix. Concern: artifact assumes a 48 GB A40 so SDXL-class models need scale-down or offload on 24 GB

title: AQETuner: Reliable Query-level Configuration Tuning for Analytical Query Engines
note: Bayesian-optimization query-level knob tuner for analytical engines - ML-based system tuning. Concern: tuning campaigns are long-running

title: DeltaZip: Efficient Serving of Multiple Full-Model-Tuned LLMs
note: Delta compression so many full-parameter fine-tuned models share one GPU; the system is explicitly single-GPU multi-tenant serving. AE Available plus Functional plus Reproduced. Concern - custom CUDA quantization kernels must build for compute capability 8.6, and several fine-tuned 7B checkpoints are needed on the 257 GB of free disk

title: Fast, Approximate Vector Queries on Very Large Unstructured Datasets
note: Vector query engine that builds a per-query error-latency profile - the single-worker path is the interesting mechanism and runs in user space - Concern: headline numbers use DEEP1B on four c5.metal instances so experiments must be scaled to SIFT or GIST million-to-100M datasets to fit 125 GiB RAM and 257 GB disk

title: Efficient Multimodal Serving via Module Multiplexing
note: Module multiplexing scheduler for multimodal model serving - concurrent scheduling of encoder and LLM modules on one GPU is directly reproducible at small scale. No code found yet

title: Collaborative Text Editing with Eg-walker: Better, Faster, Smaller
note: Collaborative editing algorithm in Rust with a single-process benchmark harness measuring CPU time and memory only - zero hardware dependencies. AE Available plus Functional plus Reproduced. Concern - needs a Rust toolchain via rustup in $HOME, otherwise nothing on the exclusion list applies

title: KTransformers: Unleashing the Full Potential of CPU/GPU Hybrid Inference for MoE Models
note: A single-GPU-plus-large-DRAM system by construction - the exact shape of this machine (1x24 GB GPU, 125 GB RAM). The Expert Deferral mechanism and the async CPU-GPU scheduler are hardware-agnostic and directly improvable. Very actively maintained (19.5k stars). Concerns - the headline CPU kernels are Intel AMX-specific and this is an AMD Zen3 Threadripper with no AMX and no AVX-512, so the CPU-side speedups will not reproduce as published; and 671B DeepSeek-V3/R1 needs far more than 125 GB, so a smaller MoE (e.g. Mixtral-class or Qwen3-MoE) scale-down is required.

title: Breaking the Reward Barrier: Accelerating Tree-of-Thought Reasoning via Speculative Exploration
note: Speculative exploration of Tree-of-Thought branches to break the reward-synchronisation barrier - a serving-layer scheduling change, testable with one GPU. Concern: the paper's model set includes Llemma-34B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, which do not fit 24 GB; only the 7B/8B configurations are reachable (possibly with quantization)

title: NetDiffusion: Network Data Augmentation Through Protocol-Constrained Traffic Generation
note: A user-space generative data pipeline: a fine-tuned Stable Diffusion plus ControlNet model with protocol-constraint post-processing, sized for a single consumer GPU, so a 24 GB A5000 is sufficient for both fine-tuning (LoRA) and inference; the repo is popular and maintained, and generation cost per trace is the paper's acknowledged weak point, which makes a performance-improvement hypothesis natural. Concern: topic fit is the weakest in this list - it is generative ML applied to networking data rather than a core systems artifact, so the audit may prefer to drop it. Second concern: FlashAttention-2 works on Ampere but FP8 kernels do not, which caps some inference-speedup options.

title: Neuralink: Fast on-Device LLM Inference with Neuron Co-Activation Linking
note: Co-activation-aware neuron placement in flash for sparse on-device LLM inference; the placement/caching idea transfers to NVMe-backed offloaded inference; concerns: original evaluation targets smartphone flash IOPS and no official repo was found

title: On Scalable Integrity Checking for Secure Cloud Disks
note: Dynamic Merkle Trees are a 5 KLoC user-space C++ data structure on the storage I/O path, driven by synthetic Zipfian and real Alibaba block traces - the algorithmic contribution is reproducible without privileges. Concerns - the paper's block-device integration uses BDUS, which ships an out-of-tree kernel module that cannot be loaded without root; the experiment harness would have to be re-hosted on FUSE or on a pure user-space trace replayer, which changes the absolute numbers.

title: Unified Static–Dynamic Pruning for Efficient LLM Inference
note: Unified static and dynamic weight pruning with custom CUDA-core and Tensor-Core kernels. Concern: kernels are tuned for newer inference GPUs so Ampere performance must be re-measured

title: FlashInfer-Bench: Building the Virtuous Cycle for AI-driven LLM Systems
note: Closed-loop harness for LLM-generated GPU kernels with correctness/performance checks and hot-swap into vLLM or SGLang; a single GPU is enough to run the loop. Concerns: several curated traces and reference kernels assume Hopper-class features that Ampere lacks, and agent runs need paid LLM API budget

title: Fairness in Serving Large Language Models
note: Virtual Token Counter fair-queueing scheduler for LLM serving - a scheduling policy layered on a serving engine which is cheap to reproduce and extend on one GPU with small models

title: Heuristic Analysis from Source Code via Symbolic-Guided Optimization
note: Analyzes a heuristic's source code directly with symbolic-guided search to find worst-case inputs - CPU-only user-space tool, released by Microsoft. Concern - the demo domains are traffic engineering and VM placement, so topic fit with the course is indirect; the contribution is the analysis engine, not the network.

title: HedraRAG: Co-Optimizing Generation and Retrieval for Heterogeneous RAG Workflows
note: Graph-based scheduling of RAG stages onto a single CPU-GPU pipeline - exactly the single-node, single-GPU setting of this machine. Concerns - retrieval index and corpus size must fit in 257 GB of free disk; generator model must be scaled to 7-8B FP16 to fit 24 GB.

title: Brook-2PL: Tolerating High Contention Workloads with A Deadlock-Free Two-Phase Locking Protocol
note: deadlock-free two-phase-locking protocol with partial transaction chopping - user-space concurrency-control mechanism benchmarked with TPC-C - concern: no repo located

title: Loom: Efficient Capture and Querying of High-Frequency Telemetry
note: Self-contained Rust ingest-plus-sparse-index engine; the repo's usage/ examples drive it with synthetic record generators (rand/rand_distr) rather than live tracers, so the ingest-throughput and query-latency claims are reproducible without any privileged data source. Baselines FishStore and InfluxDB both install in user space. Concerns - the paper's motivating data sources (perf, DTrace, eBPF) are all blocked on this machine, so evaluation must use synthetic or pre-recorded traces, which weakens realism.

title: Better than Optimal: Improving Adaptive Stochastic Quantization Using Shared Randomness
note: Adaptive unbiased quantization with shared randomness for gradient and tensor compression. Self-contained numeric code plus a distributed-mean-estimation case study that runs fine as multiple processes on one box; no special hardware

title: Machine Unlearning in Learned Databases: An Experimental Analysis
note: Experimental analysis of unlearning/update handling in learned DB components (cardinality estimation, learned indexes); CPU+1 GPU is enough. Concern: no repo found in GitHub search

title: Why Are Learned Indexes So Effective but Sometimes Ineffective?
note: Analysis of why PGM learned indexes under-perform plus PGM++; in-memory user-space benchmark, directly improvable
